sanskrit: paraḥ so astu tanvā tanā ca tisraḥ pṛthivīr adho astu viśvāḥ | prati śuṣyati yaśo asya devā yo mā divā dipsati yaś ca naktam ||
english: May he be cut off — body and offspring — and may all three earths lie beneath him. His glory withers away, O gods, whoever seeks to harm me by day and whoever seeks to harm me by night.

sanskrit: suvijñānaṃ cikituṣe janāya sac cāsac ca vacasī paspṛśāte | tayor yat satyaṃ yatarad ṛjīyas tad it somo 'vati hanty āsat ||
english: To the person of discernment it is well known: the words of truth and falsehood touch each other. Of these two, whichever is true, whichever is the more upright — that one Soma protects; the false he strikes down.

sanskrit: na vā u somo vṛjinaṃ hinoti na kṣatriyaṃ mithuyā dhārayantam | hanti rakṣo hanty āsad vadantam ubhāv indrasya prasitau śayāte ||
english: Soma does not drive forward the crooked, nor the kṣatriya who bears false office. He slays the rakṣas; he slays the speaker of falsehood — both lie in Indra's snare.

sanskrit: yadi vāham anṛtadevo asmi moghaṃ vā devām̐ apyūhe agne | kim asmabhyaṃ jātavedo hṛṇīṣe droghavācas te nirṛthaṃ sacantām ||
english: If indeed I am one who makes a god of falsehood, or if I invoke the gods in vain, O Agni — why then art thou angry with us, O Jātaveda? Let them who speak treachery cleave to Nirṛti without purpose.

sanskrit: adyā murīya yadi yātudhāno asmi yadi vāyus tatapa pūruṣasya | adhā sa vīrair daśabhir vi yūyā yo mā moghaṃ yātudhānety aha ||
english: May I die this very day if I am a yātudhāna, or if the breath of a man has been scorched by me. But let him who calls me a yātudhāna falsely be scattered apart with his ten heroes.

sanskrit: yo māyātuṃ yātudhānety āha yo mā rakṣāḥ śucir asmīty āha | indras taṃ hantu mahatā vadhena viśvasya jantor adhamas padīṣṭa ||
english: Whoever says to me 'thou art a sorcerer, a yātudhāna,' whoever, being a rakṣas himself, says 'I am pure' — may Indra smite him with a great blow; may he fall the lowest of all living creatures.

sanskrit: pra yā jigāti khargaleva naktam apa druhus tanvaṃ gūhamānā | vavrām̐ anantām̐ ava sā padīṣṭa grāvāṇo ghnantu rakṣasa upabdaiḥ ||
english: She who moves abroad at night like a screech-owl, concealing her treacherous body — may she fall down into endless pits; may the pressing-stones smite the rakṣas with their thunder.

sanskrit: vi tiṣṭhadhvaṃ maruto vikṣv icchata gṛbhāyata rakṣasaḥ saṃ pinaṣṭana | vayo ye bhūtvā patayanti naktabhir ye vā ripo dadhire deve adhvare ||
english: Spread out, O Maruts; search through the settlements; seize the rakṣases, crush them together. Those who take the forms of birds and fly through the nights, or those who have set deception within the divine sacrifice — crush them.

sanskrit: eta u tye patayanti śvayātava indraṃ dipsanti dipsavo 'dābhyam | śiśīte śakraḥ piśunebhyo vadhaṃ nūnaṃ sṛjad aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
english: Here they come flying, the dog-roving ones; the deceivers seek to deceive Indra, the undecievable. Śakra sharpens his weapon against the slanderers; now will he loose his thunderbolt against the sorcerers.

sanskrit: pra vartaya divo aśmānam indra somaśitaṃ maghavan saṃ śiśādhi | prākto apākto adharād udakto abhi jahi rakṣasaḥ parvatena ||
english: Roll forth the stone of heaven, O Indra; sharpen it well, O Maghavan, whetted by Soma. From the east, from the west, from below, from above — smite the rakṣases with the mountain.

sanskrit: indro yātūnām abhavat parāśaro havirmathīnām abhy āvivāsatām | abhīd u śakraḥ paraśur yathā vanaṃ pātreva bhindant sata eti rakṣasaḥ ||
english: Indra became Parāśara against the yātu-sorcerers, against those who churn away the oblation. Śakra indeed advances like an axe through a forest, splitting the rakṣases by the hundreds like vessels.

sanskrit: ulūkayātuṃ śuśulūkayātuṃ jahi śvayātum uta kokayātum | suparṇayātum uta gṛdhrayātuṃ dṛṣadeva pra mṛṇa rakṣa indra ||
english: Slay the owl-sorcerer and the screech-owl-sorcerer; slay the dog-sorcerer and the kokay-bird-sorcerer; slay the eagle-sorcerer and the vulture-sorcerer — crush the rakṣas, O Indra, as with a pressing-stone.

sanskrit: mā no rakṣo abhi naḍ yātumāvatām apocchataṃ mithunā yā kimīdinā | pṛthivī naḥ pārthivāt pātv aṃhaso antarikṣaṃ divyāt pātv asmān ||
english: Let no rakṣas, none possessed by yātu-sorcery, press upon us. Drive away the coupled Kimīdins. May the Earth protect us from earthly distress; may the Atmosphere protect us from the heavenly.

sanskrit: indra jahi pumāṃsaṃ yātudhānam uta striyaṃ māyayā śāśadānām | vigrīvāso mūradevā rudantu mā te dṛśan sūryam uccarantam ||
english: O Indra, smite the male yātudhāna and also the female who injures through sorcery. Let those with broken necks, the god-bereft, weep; may they not behold the sun as it rises.

sanskrit: prati cakṣva vi cakṣva- -indraś ca soma jāgṛtam | rakṣobhyo vadham asyatam aśaniṃ yātumadbhyaḥ ||
english: Keep watch, keep vigil — O Indra and Soma, be awake! Hurl the weapon of death upon the rakṣases; hurl the thunderbolt upon the sorcerers.

sanskrit: yā babhravo yāś ca śukrā rohiṇīr uta pṛśnayaḥ | asiknīḥ kṛṣṇā oṣadhīḥ sarvā acchā vadāmasi ||
english: The brown ones and the bright ones, the red ones and the dappled ones, the dark ones, the black plants — to all these healing herbs we now speak out.

sanskrit: trāyantām imaṃ puruṣaṃ yakṣmād deveṣitād adhi | yāsāṃ dyauṣ pitā pṛthivī mātā samudro mūlaṃ vīrudhāṃ babhūva ||
english: May they protect this man from the yakṣma disease sent by the gods — those whose father is Dyaus, whose mother is Pṛthivī, and whose root has become the ocean.

sanskrit: āpo 'graṃ divyā oṣadhhayas | tās te yakṣmam enasyam aṅgādaṅgād anīnaśan ||
english: The divine waters are foremost among the healing herbs. They have driven out the sin-laden yakṣma from your limb by limb.

sanskrit: prastṛṇatī stambinīr ekaśṛṅgāḥ pratanvatīr oṣadhīr ā vadāmi | aṃśumatīḥ kāṇḍinīr yā viśākhā hvayāmi te vīrudho vaiśvadevīr ugrāḥ puruṣajīvanīḥ ||
english: I address the spreading plants, the clumping ones, the single-stemmed, the creeping herbs. I call you — the filamentous, the jointed, those with spreading branches — those plants that belong to all the gods, the potent, the life-sustaining for man.

sanskrit: yad vaḥ sahaḥ sahamānā vīryaṃ yac ca vo balam | tenemam asmād yakṣmāt puruṣaṃ muñcantauṣadhīḥ ||
english: By that power of yours, O herbs, which overpowers, by the virile force and strength that is in you — with that, release this man from this yakṣma disease.

sanskrit: jīvalāṃ naghāriṣāṃ jīvantīm oṣadhīm uta | arundhatīm unnayantīṃ puṣpāṃ madhumatīṃ huve ||
english: I invoke Jīvalā, Naghāriṣā, the living herb, and Arundhatī the uplifting, the flowering one, the honey-sweet one.

sanskrit: ihā yantu pracetaso medinīr vacaso mama | yathemaṃ pārayāmasi puruṣaṃ duritād adhi ||
english: May the wise, the knowing ones come here at my word, so that we may carry this man across, beyond misfortune.

sanskrit: agner ghāso apāṃ garbho yā rohanti punarṇavāḥ | dhruvāḥ sahasranāmnīr bheṣajīḥ santv ābhṛtāḥ ||
english: The food of Agni, the embryo of the waters — those that grow anew as punarṇavās: may those steadfast, thousand-named healing plants be gathered and brought here.

sanskrit: avakolvā udakātmāna oṣadhayaḥ | vyajṛṣantī duritaṃ tīkṣṇaśṛṅgyaḥ ||
english: The herbs that dwell in hollows, whose nature is water, the sharp-horned ones — shaking off all misfortune, they drive it away.

sanskrit: unmuñcantīr vivaruṇā ugrā yā viṣadūṣaṇīr atho balāsanāśanīḥ | rakṣonāśanīḥ kṛtyādūṣaṇīś ca yās tā ihā yantv oṣadhīḥ ||
english: Those that release bonds, the wide-opening ones, the fierce ones that destroy poison, and those that destroy the balāsa affliction, those that destroy rakṣases, that neutralize kṛtyā witchcraft — may those herbs come here.
